boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Cedar Creek record (October 19, 1864) in Sheridan's Valley Campaign [August-October 1864]. The October 13 reconnaissance at Hupp's Hill and the October 20 pursuit are context. Campaign-wide marches, destruction, reinforcements, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads 52,945 total (US 31,945; CS 21,000); the live field reads 47210 (US 31945; CS 15265). Pond says Early had received reinforcements of nearly 5,000 exclusive of the Valley reserves, and that although his army was smaller than Sheridan's he had the stronger force at each point of attack. Early wrote on October 9 that without Kershaw he had about 6,000 muskets.
claims.rationale: The frozen and live Confederate figures differ by 5,735 and no source basis is given; Early's October 9 figure excludes Kershaw and predates the battle by ten days. None is adopted as a matched opening strength.

claims.value: Pond says Wright, as senior officer, was left in charge while Sheridan went to Washington; that Wright ordered the cavalry to the left during the morning; and that Sheridan, returning from Winchester, formed the line and ordered the 4 p.m. advance. Early says he had cautioned his division commanders against plundering; Pond quotes Early that Kershaw reported his division not in a condition to attack. The frozen commanders are Lieutenant General Early and Major Generals Horatio Wright and Philip Sheridan; the live page lists Wright only.
claims.rationale: Command roles from a history and an interested report; command passed during the day, and no listed commander receives automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen result reads Union victory and the live result Union Victory. Early says he surprised and routed the Eighth and Nineteenth Corps and drove the Sixth, but his left gave way to the counterattack and the rest panicked, a rout as thorough as any his army had suffered; Pond says the Union counterattack produced the greatest rout since Bull Run.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 8,575 total (US 5,665; CS 2,910); the live field reads 7682 (US 5672; CS 2010). Pond gives the Union loss as 5,764 and Early's as about 3,100, 1,860 killed and wounded with something over 1,000 prisoners by Early's account, about 1,200 taken by Sheridan; Early kept 1,429 prisoners. Early's dispatches claim 1,300 prisoners, a net loss of twenty-three guns, killed and wounded less than 1,000 in one and not more than 700 or 800 in another. Pond says 24 Confederate guns were captured.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Early's opening report pages (561-562) are missing from this OCR.

open_questions: Early's October 21 report pages 561-562 are missing from this OCR; a second scan of Volume XLIII Part 1 was not sought. Sheridan's 1866 report passage on the battle (read, not selected), his October 19 dispatch, Wright's, Emory's, Crook's, Torbert's, Getty's and Custer's reports, Grimes's and Kershaw's brigade reports, the compiled Union return (No. 7) and Hotchkiss's journal remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. George E. Pond's The Shenandoah Valley in 1864 (Scribner, 1883) is a retrospective history written, by its preface, from the official documents at the War Records Office and field despatches; it quotes Sheridan's, Torbert's, Wright's and Early's reports and despatches and is not independent of them. Early's reports and dispatches of September 23-October 21, 1864 to Lee are one family of interested Confederate accounts; it is the same author family as his July 14 report selected for Early's Raid. Official Records Series I, Volume XLIII, Part 1 is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
